did_you_know.text: Did you know? The phrase "Shlach Lecha" (send for yourself) in God's command to Moses implies that while God permitted the mission, it was primarily for the people's reassurance and benefit, not an essential divine command.

Did you know? The spies were sent from the Wilderness of Paran, a vast and desolate region in the northern Sinai Peninsula, which served as a significant staging area for the Israelites before entering Canaan.

Did you know? Moses changed Hoshea's name to Yehoshua (Joshua). The addition of the letter Yud (י) to "Hoshea" (salvation) made it "Yehoshua" (God saves), likely as a prayer that God would save him from the spies' wicked counsel.
Did you know? Moses instructed the spies to enter Canaan "through the Negev," which is the arid southern region of Israel, known for its challenging desert terrain even today.
Did you know? The mission took place during "the days of the first ripe grapes," indicating late summer (July-August). This timing ensured they would see the land at its most fertile and productive.
Did you know? The spies encountered the "children of Anak" (Anakim), a race of giants whose imposing stature terrified the spies and contributed to their negative report.

Did you know? The verse mentions that Hebron was built seven years before Zoan of Egypt. Zoan (Tanis) was a major ancient city and capital in the Nile Delta, making Hebron's age a testament to its very deep historical roots.
Did you know? The spies brought back a single cluster of grapes so large that it required two men to carry it on a pole. This vividly demonstrated the land's extraordinary fertility and abundance.
Did you know? The place where the spies cut the giant grape cluster was named "Nahal Eshkol" (Valley of the Cluster) because of this very event, a name still used in the region today.

Did you know? The spy mission lasted exactly forty days. The number 40 often appears in the Bible as a period of testing, purification, or judgment, such as the 40 days of the flood or the 40 years in the desert.

Did you know? Only Caleb, out of the ten fearful spies, silenced the people and urged them to go up and conquer the land, expressing unwavering faith in their ability to do so, despite the challenges.
